newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares strong, players keep fingers crossed.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares strong, players keep fingers crossed.

text.p: Belgian shares shrugged off a hesitant start on Wall Street to close near the intraday highs but dealers said only more convincing performances in New York could prevent nervousness from spreading.
The Bel-20 index ended 0.64 percent, or 13.74 points, higher at 2,147.34 in a tight 2,138-2150 range with about three billion francs worth of Belgian shares traded.
"It looks as if the impact of U.S. data and Wall Street is waning a bit," one trader said. "People are becoming more and more wary and are always looking for clearer signals," he said.
Insurance firm Fortis AG was the day's star performer with a 2.7 percent jump to 6,000 francs, but one dealer said it notched up the bulk of its gains near the close.

In an interview in the Cash investment magazine, Generale Bank's Luc Van der Elst included AG in his list of buy candidates. Van der Elst believed that fundamentally the Brussels bourse was not expensive yet.

Petrofina was also included in Generale Bank's list. The oil group was the market leader in volume terms but shed 0.4 percent to 12,725 on mild profit-taking after its jump of more than six percent in the past two days.
PVC profiles producer Deceuninck was the day's biggest loser with a 2.4 percent slide to 6,610 despite enjoying a buy recommendation from Vermeulen-Raemdonck.
In its latest share research reports, KB-Securities brokerage advised reducing the weight of natural gas company Distrigas but adding shares in cement maker CBR in portfolio.
